assessments.reasoning: Part 1 of the digest-pinned Automake file contains both dispositive passages. Each has its own subject and scope. The redistribution and modification clause names the macro file and expressly allows a later version. The result-use clause specifies TeX reading that file while processing a Texinfo source document.

As context, the pinned generated entry reproduces the section 7 designation and identifies the location of the permission in the GNU file. It omits the preceding file-license paragraph, so the or-later election depends on direct inspection of that paragraph. The two sources agree within their respective scopes.

challenge.method: I tested GPL-3.0-only against the complete version-election sentence and checked whether SPDX’s reference to version 3 or the file’s UTF-8 component attribution supplied a competing base notice.
challenge.results: GPL-3.0-only would omit the holder’s express later-version option. The section 7 sentence names the edition under which the additional permission is designated. The UTF-8 attribution describes inclusion of that component under the GPL and gives no competing file-wide version election.

limitations: The finding describes this header. It does not decide the legal effect of electing a later GPL version or the licensing of a particular document or output.
The named sources establish the base variant in words. Resolution of the opaque local target f6c5ffa485db43d9ad2d2898bf30b86f to a registry entity was not independently verified.
reasoning: Lines 10–13 expressly permit redistribution or modification of “This texinfo.tex file” under the GNU General Public License as published by the Free Software Foundation, “either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.” That election supports GPL-3.0-or-later for this specimen. Lines 23–26 separately identify the conditional TeX processing permission as a GPLv3 section 7 additional permission.
